title: The world's alphabet
description: There is no single alphabet for all languages, but the IPA (International Phonetic Alphabet) is a phonetic alphabet with one symbol for each sound.

title: The hardest language is Mandarin Chinese
description: Mandarin Chinese uses characters; to hold a conversation or read a newspaper, knowing at least 3,000 characters is helpful. It also has four tones to distinguish words with the same syllables. However, how hard a language feels depends on your native language.

title: The longest word in the world
description: Linguists do not fully agree on the longest word overall, but the English term "Pneumonoultramicroscopicsilicovolcanoconiosis" (45 letters) is certainly among the longest. It names a lung disease caused by inhaling silica dust from a volcano.

title: Some of the oldest languages are still used today
description: The earliest documented languages (Sumerian, Egyptian, Akkadian, Eblaite) have disappeared. However, very ancient languages are still in use, such as Chinese (first written attestations around 1200 BCE), Hebrew (10th century BCE), and Greek (attested since the 8th century BCE).

title: The Cambodian alphabet is the longest
description: The Cambodian (Khmer) alphabet has 74 characters, making it one of the longest in the world.

title: Over 300 languages in London
description: In London, besides English, more than 300 different languages are spoken.

title: Hawaiians have over 200 words for "rain"
description: In some languages there are many words for the color white; in Hawaii there are over 200 different words to describe rain.

title: The most polyglot person speaks 59 languages
description: Lebanese Ziad Youssef Fazah claims to speak 59 languages and entered the Guinness World Records as the person who speaks the most languages.

title: The longest book in the world
description: Written by French author Marcel Proust, the novel "In Search of Lost Time" is a vast journey through time and memory.

title: The largest private book collection
description: John Q. Benham, who lives in the state of Indiana (United States), holds the record for the largest private book collection in the world: about 1.5 million volumes.

title: A novel without the letter E
description: Lipograms are texts written while avoiding a particular letter. "Gadsby" is a 1939 novel by Ernest Vincent Wright in which the letter "e" is never used.

title: The most expensive book ever sold
description: The Codex Leicester is the most expensive book ever sold: Bill Gates purchased it in 1994 for about 30 million dollars. It collects notes, drawings, and writings by Leonardo da Vinci.

title: The shortest short story
description: Augusto Monterroso wrote one of the shortest stories ever: "When he woke up, the dinosaur was still there." A single sentence that suggests an entire story.

title: The best-selling book in history
description: The Harry Potter series is among the best-selling, but the best-selling book of all time is the Bible, with billions of copies distributed.

title: The basket building
description: The Basket Building in Newark, Ohio, is a giant basket-shaped building. It was the headquarters of a basket-making company; in 2016 the company moved and the building was put up for sale.

title: The tower rising from the lake
description: In Lake Resia, in South Tyrol, the top of a bell tower emerges from the surface: it is the only visible part of the village of Curon, submerged in 1950 for a hydroelectric plant.

title: Toronto’s half house, Canada
description: Built in the late 19th century, it was part of a row of townhouses. The others were demolished to make room for new buildings; this half house remained because the owners refused to sell.

title: The largest airport in the world
description: King Fahd International Airport in Dammam, Saudi Arabia, is among the largest by area: about 776 km², almost as large as New York City.

title: The hotel made of ice
description: The Icehotel in Jukkasjärvi, Sweden, is built entirely of ice. It was the world’s first ice hotel and is rebuilt every year in the same place.

title: The smallest house in Italy
description: In the center of Rome, near the Pantheon, there is a two-level studio of just 7 m². The owner, an architect, lived there for a few years with his wife.

title: Italy’s tallest skyscraper
description: The UniCredit Tower in Milan, 231 meters tall and inaugurated in 2014, is the tallest skyscraper in Italy.

title: The tallest skyscraper in the world
description: At 829 meters, the Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest skyscraper in the world: almost twice the height of New York’s Empire State Building.

title: No bathroom allowed
description: In Tidong, Indonesia, newlyweds are not allowed to use the bathroom for the three days following the wedding: by superstition, breaking the rule would bring bad luck to the couple.

title: Polterabend in Germany
description: In Germany, shortly before the wedding, family and friends gather to break plates and dishes (but not glasses). Then the couple has to clean up: it symbolizes the joint effort needed to make a marriage work.

title: See you at the cemetery
description: In Denmark, cemeteries are considered parks: places to walk on sunny days and relax, maintained like public green areas.

title: The meaning of the thumbs-up
description: Showing a thumbs-up in many countries means "like" or "OK". But gestures vary across cultures: in Iraq and Iran this gesture has a very negative meaning, comparable to the middle finger.

title: Chasing the rolling cheese
description: Near the English village of Brockworth, Cooper's Hill Cheese-Rolling and Wake is held: participants, in groups, chase a large wheel of cheese rolling down a hill.

title: Boot throwing
description: In Finland, boot throwing has been practiced for generations: whoever throws it the farthest wins.

title: A game of human chess
description: In Marostica (VI), every two years in September a chess match is played with people instead of pieces.

title: Llanfairpwllgwyngyllgogerychwyrndrobwllllantysiliogogogoch: the longest place name
description: It is a small village in Wales, UK, famous for the length of its name. It is also mentioned in a 1970 Mickey Mouse story. Locals often call it "Llanfair PG".

title: The original name of Los Angeles
description: The city’s original name was "El Pueblo de Nuestra Señora la Reina de los Ángeles de Porciúncula".

title: Rats are ticklish
description: Rats are sensitive to tickling: there are educational videos that clearly show it.

title: What pigs cannot do
description: Unlike cows and horses, it is physically very difficult for a pig to look upward.

title: Elephants’ funerals
description: In the wild, elephants show caring behavior toward their dead: they cover bodies with leaves and branches and return to visit them.

title: The deadliest animal in the world
description: It is neither the lion nor the alligator: the deadliest animal is the mosquito. According to the WHO, every year hundreds of thousands of people die from mosquito-borne diseases (malaria, dengue, yellow fever).

title: A cockroach can live without its head
description: Cockroaches can survive for weeks without a head, and the head can remain vital for a few hours separated from the body.

title: A tongue as heavy as an elephant
description: The blue whale’s tongue can weigh as much as a small adult elephant: over 3,000 kg.

title: The flea’s jump
description: The flea is a jumping champion: it can jump up to 200 times its own length (about 25 cm vertically and 45 cm horizontally). In proportion, it would be like a human jumping to the top of the Empire State Building.

title: The loudest land animal
description: The howler monkey is the loudest land animal: its calls can be heard up to 5 km away and can reach about 140 decibels, comparable to a jet taking off.

title: Skin renews in about a month
description: We lose around 40,000 skin cells every day: over about a month, the skin renews almost completely.

title: Trees communicate
description: Plants communicate through a network of roots and mycorrhizal fungi, sometimes called the "Wood Wide Web": trees can transfer nutrients and signaling substances.

title: Why we smile in photos
description: In early 20th-century photographs people rarely smiled. The habit of smiling in photos spread partly thanks to Kodak’s advertising.

title: Hot water can freeze before cold water
description: This is the Mpemba effect: under some conditions, hotter water can freeze before colder water.

title: Why we blink
description: Blinking lubricates the eye and, according to some research, gives the brain micro-breaks of a few moments to recharge.

title: The seed vault
description: In the Svalbard archipelago, between Norway and the North Pole, lies the Svalbard Global Seed Vault: a "fortress" that safeguards the world’s largest collection of seeds.

title: Tongue print
description: The pattern of one’s tongue is unique for each individual, just like fingerprints.

title: There are no perfectly straight lines
description: When you magnify anything enough, irregularities emerge: even laser beams show slight curvature and imperfections.

title: Contortions
description: For most people it is impossible to lick their elbow. Can you do it?
